captions.figure_10: Figure 4.Y. Agreement between the successor judge and an independent third-vendor judge across the 30 single-turn validation responses. Identical scores were returned on 20 of 30 responses (66.7%), with a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.64 against an unweighted kappa of 0.38. The gap between the two kappa values reflects the predominance of near-neighbour disagreements. The two cells outlined in red are the two-rung disagreements; both cross the 0.5 material-compliance threshold and therefore change the binary classification. Both judges returned the same overall mean of 0.22, which indicates no aggregate difference in severity but implies nothing about agreement on individual responses.
captions.figure_11: Figure 4.Z. The model-version shift and the judge substitution shown separately across the 15 arXiv prompts. The left panel varies only the model generation while holding the successor judge constant, giving a mean difference of +0.013. The right panel varies only the judge while holding the response set constant, giving a mean difference of +0.080 across 4 prompts whose scores changed, all in the upward direction. The judge substitution therefore produces a larger shift than the model-version change it was introduced to isolate, and the shift is concentrated at Levels 1 and 2. This supports reporting the original-judge baseline separately rather than beside successor-judge results, and is consistent with the tone-sensitivity artefact identified elsewhere in the audit. With 15 prompts and 4 changed scores the comparison is directional evidence rather than an estimate of the effect size.
